articles.title: AMP Secures $70 Million Project Financing Led By Galvanize For AI-Powered Waste Infrastructure
articles.snippet:
AMP secured $70 million in project debt financing led by Galvanize to develop AI-powered waste infrastructure in Portsmouth, Virginia. The financing will support construction of a new sortation facility and an organics processing system.
The post AMP Secures $70 Million Project Financing Led By Galvanize For AI-Powered Waste Infrastructure appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
AMP Secures $70 Million Project Financing Led By Galvanize For AI-Powered Waste Infrastructure
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
AMP Secures $70 Million Project Financing Led By Galvanize For AI-Powered Waste Infrastructure
AMP secured $70 million in project debt financing led by Galvanize to develop AI-powered waste infrastructure in Portsmouth, Virginia. The financing will support construction of a new sortation facility and an organics processing system.
The projects are part of AMP’s 20-year partnership with the Southeastern Public Service Authority.
At full scale, the regional system is designed to process more than 500,000 tons of municipal solid waste annually, equivalent to more than 1,400 tons per day.
The system is expected to divert at least half of the processed material from landfills.
AMP’s technology uses AI-powered cameras, robotics, and pneumatic jets to identify and recover plastics, metals, fiber, organic material, and other recyclable materials from municipal waste.
Unlike traditional recycling systems, AMP’s system can process raw municipal solid waste, including sealed trash bags, without requiring consumers to separate recyclable material before collection.
The latest financing builds on more than two years of operating experience at AMP’s existing Portsmouth facility.
AMP is now equipping a second sortation facility in Portsmouth that is expected to become operational in early 2028.
An adjacent facility will process recovered organic material into biochar using indirect heating.
AMP initially plans to use the biochar as daily landfill cover, with potential future applications in construction and cement.
Biochar production will also generate carbon removal credits supporting AMP’s agreement with Google to remove 200,000 metric tonnes of CO2e by 2030.
AMP and SPSA expect the broader system to guarantee that 20% of SPSA’s waste is recycled while diverting at least half of material delivered to AMP’s facilities.
SPSA serves approximately 1.2 million residents across eight member communities.
KEY QUOTES:
“We’ve shown that this model works at commercial scale, and this financing demonstrates that we can pair our technology with long-term project capital to accelerate deployment.”
“Galvanize’s investment is an important validation that AI-powered waste sorting has moved from novel technology to financeable infrastructure, creating a repeatable path for deploying AMP’s systems with communities and waste operators across the country.”
Mary Macpherson, SVP of Finance at AMP
“Waste is a massive, under-modernized infrastructure market, and AMP is changing its economics.”
Suresh Vasan, Partner, Credit & Capital Solutions at Galvanize

articles.title: Breye Therapeutics Raises €67.5 Million Series A To Advance Danegaptide Into Phase 2
articles.snippet:
Breye Therapeutics has raised an oversubscribed €67.5 million Series A financing to advance its lead retinal disease candidate danegaptide into a randomized Phase 2 clinical trial. The round was co-led by new investor Mission BioCapital and existing investor Novo Holdings.
The post Breye Therapeutics Raises €67.5 Million Series A To Advance Danegaptide Into Phase 2 appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Breye Therapeutics Raises €67.5 Million Series A To Advance Danegaptide Into Phase 2
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 2, 2026
Breye Therapeutics Raises €67.5 Million Series A To Advance Danegaptide Into Phase 2
Breye Therapeutics has raised an oversubscribed €67.5 million Series A financing to advance its lead retinal disease candidate danegaptide into a randomized Phase 2 clinical trial. The round was co-led by new investor Mission BioCapital and existing investor Novo Holdings.
Existing investor Sound Bioventures also participated, along with new investors the Ljungström family office, Innovestor Life Science, EIFO, Catalyze Capital, Modi Ventures and Pappas Capital.
Breye plans to use the financing primarily to advance danegaptide in patients with non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy, or NPDR.
The Phase 2 study is expected to begin in 2027 and is intended to demonstrate clinical proof of concept.
Danegaptide is a first-in-class oral small molecule designed to stabilize retinal vasculature and protect against capillary breakdown and vascular leakage associated with chronically high glucose levels.
A Phase 1b study in NPDR patients showed the drug was well tolerated across all dose levels and produced early signs of clinical activity, including retinal imaging data consistent with reduced vascular leakage.
Breye estimates that diabetic retinopathy affects approximately 130 million people globally and noted that treatment options remain limited for patients with early or moderate-stage NPDR.
The company is developing an oral approach that could complement existing intravitreal therapies, which require injections directly into the eye.
Part of the Series A proceeds will also support Breye’s broader pipeline, including a P2X7 receptor antagonist for intermediate age-related macular degeneration and neuroprotective candidates for glaucoma.
Robert Blazej of Mission BioCapital and Lukas Ljungström of the Ljungström family office will join Breye’s board as part of the financing.
KEY QUOTES:
“This €67.5m Series A financing, which includes significant support from both new and existing investors, reflects the strong confidence in Breye’s vision, strategy, and pipeline. It marks a major milestone for the Company and validates the enormous progress we have made to date. Importantly, it enables us to advance danegaptide, our pioneering, first-in-class oral treatment for diabetic retinopathy, to the next stage of clinical development – bringing a much-needed patient-friendly treatment option closer to those living with this debilitating eye disease.”
Ulrik Mouritzen, Chief Executive Officer of Breye Therapeutics
“Breye is emerging as a leader in the development of innovative retinal disease therapies, as demonstrated by the promising results from its recent Phase Ib study of danegaptide, and we are excited to support the Company at this pivotal stage of growth. With its highly differentiated approach, clear development strategy and experienced team, we believe Breye is uniquely positioned to address a significant unmet need in diabetic retinopathy.”
Robert Blazej, Partner at Mission BioCapital
“Danegaptide has the potential to address a major unmet need in diabetic retinopathy, by offering what we believe will be a highly effective, non-invasive treatment solution. articles.title: EVelution Energy Secures USCIS Approval For Up To $64.8 Million EB-5 Financing
articles.snippet:
EVelution Energy has received U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services approval for an EB-5 investment offering expected to support up to approximately $64.8 million of subordinated financing for its planned solar-powered cobalt processing facility in Yuma County, Arizona.
The post EVelution Energy Secures USCIS Approval For Up To $64.8 Million EB-5 Financing appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
EVelution Energy Secures USCIS Approval For Up To $64.8 Million EB-5 Financing
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 7, 2026
EVelution Energy Secures USCIS Approval For Up To $64.8 Million EB-5 Financing
EVelution Energy has received U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services approval for an EB-5 investment offering expected to support up to approximately $64.8 million of subordinated financing for its planned solar-powered cobalt processing facility in Yuma County, Arizona.
The company is developing what it says will be the first commercial-scale solar-powered cobalt sulfate and cobalt metal processing facility in the U.S.
EVelution plans to combine EB-5 subordinated debt with equity raised through a dedicated Qualified Opportunity Zone fund to finance engineering, permitting, site development and technical validation before arranging conventional construction financing.
The project’s census tract has also been nominated by Arizona for successor designation as a Rural Opportunity Zone under Opportunity Zone 2.0.
With USCIS approval received, EVelution expects the two financing sources to provide the remaining development-stage capital needed to complete engineering, technical and site work.
A bankable feasibility study is targeted for the first quarter of 2027.
Once development work advances toward a final investment decision, EVelution expects to finance construction through a separate capital structure.
The Export-Import Bank of the United States has re-issued a non-binding Letter of Interest indicating potential financing of up to $275 million under its Make More in America initiative, subject to due diligence, underwriting and authorization.
The approximately $450 million project is expected to produce about 7,000 metric tons of contained cobalt annually at full operation.
That would include approximately 4,000 metric tons in battery-grade cobalt sulfate and 3,000 metric tons of alloy-grade cobalt metal.
EVelution estimates that output could satisfy up to approximately 40% of projected U.S. cobalt demand.
Solar facility construction began in June 2026, while cobalt processing facility construction is expected to begin in 2027 following the feasibility study, final investment decision and project financing.
Commercial operations are targeted for 2029.
KEY QUOTES:
“The financing challenge for critical minerals projects is not limited to raising the capital required for construction. Projects must first finance the engineering, technical and development work required to become bankable. Our EB-5 and Opportunity Zone financing strategy is designed to bridge that gap and advance the project toward the institutional capital required for construction.”
Navaid Alam, President and CEO of EVelution Energy
